prompt: A distribution has a long tail on the **left**. The mean is typically:
hint: A long tail on the left means there are a few unusually small values. Think about which measure those values drag along.

hints.text: A long tail on the left means there are a few unusually small values. Think about which measure those values drag along.
The small values in the tail lower the total, so they pull the mean down toward the left. The median stays near the middle of the bulk of the data.
The mean is typically less than the median, which is choice A.

explanation: A long tail on the left means the distribution is skewed left, with a few values much smaller than the rest.
Those small values lower the sum, so the mean is pulled toward the tail.
The median depends only on the middle position, so it stays with the main group of data.
The mean therefore ends up less than the median, which is choice A.
